facts.title: Country and period
facts.text: Country: Malawi (MWI). Annual period 2014–2025, monthly series 2014-03-01 → 2022-11-01. Levels: ADM1, ADM2. Synthetic data: no.

facts.title: National trend
facts.text: Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in Malawi changed by +5.0% per year (95% CI: +2.6% to +6.8%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is -2.6% relative to the previous 12 months. (confidence high: significant trend (p < 0.01; n = 12))

facts.title: Regions
facts.text: Of 28 ADM2 units, 25 show significant growth, 3 are stagnating and 0 are declining. Light remains concentrated: Central Region accounts for 48% of national light. (confidence medium: classification of 28 units, threshold ±1%/yr and p < 0.10)

facts.title: Convergence
facts.text: Across ADM2 units, light per capita converges: the least-lit units are catching up. (confidence medium: β = −0.023 [−0.032; −0.014], n = 27)

facts.title: Link with GDP
facts.text: The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is 1.43 in levels (95% CI: 0.75 to 2.11, R² = 0.69, 12 years) and 0.56 in growth rates (CI: −3.44 to 4.56). Out of sample, light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of −0.22 (mean absolute error: 2.2 percentage points of growth). (confidence medium: n = 12, significant but wide CI (1.36))

facts.title: Shocks
facts.text: The most pronounced shock in the seasonally adjusted series is “COVID-19”: trough of +2.6% (09/2020), return to the pre-shock level after 7 months. (confidence low: trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability)

facts.title: Inequality and access
facts.text: The Gini coefficient of light per capita (ADM2) is 0.42 in 2025 (no significant change since 2014). About 0.52 million people live in inhabited areas with no detectable light (66% of the inhabited population). (confidence medium: sensitive to the radiance threshold (from 0.48 to 0.57 M depending on the threshold); a proxy for outdoor lighting, not for grid connection)

facts.title: Industrial zones
facts.text: 20 industrial clusters detected from concordant satellite signals: 11 heavy industry, 6 business parks & logistics, 1 oil & gas sites and 2 isolated sites to verify. They emit 14.0% of national light (latest year); their light changes by +2.2% per year. Southern Region has the most industrial activity. (confidence low: precision 55% and recall 27% against the reference list)

facts.title: Summer tourism
facts.text: 2 of 28 units show a net summer light excess of at least 10%: Nkhotakota (Central Region), Mzimba (Northern Region). The median net excess reaches +21% in the most touristic zone. The season index (base 100 = 2019) falls to 109 in 2020 and stands at -61 in 2025. (confidence low: correlation of -0.96 with international tourist arrivals (WDI) (4 years))

facts.title: Urbanisation
facts.text: The lit area changes by +8.6% per year, against +2.7% for population. Of 28 ADM2 units: 27 show electrified urbanisation, 1 balanced growth, 0 unlit growth. Between 2014 and 2025, 1,743 km² became lit, of which 489 km² in already inhabited areas (≈ 36k newly lit inhabitants). Largest expansion: Lilongwe (Central Region), Blantyre (Southern Region), Mangochi (Northern Region). (confidence low: rank correlation of 0.09 with GHSL built-up growth (28 units))

facts.title: Key indicators
facts.text: Annual growth of light = +5.0% (2014–2025, robust slope (Theil–Sen)); Last 12 months vs previous 12 = -2.6% (seasonally adjusted series, up to 11/2022); Light–GDP elasticity = 1.43 (95% CI 0.75 to 2.11 · confidence medium); Gini of light per capita = 0.42 (ADM2 units, 2025); People in the dark = 0.52 M (66% of the inhabited population, 2025); Share of the top region = 48% (Central Region, 2025); Industrial clusters = 20 (14% of national light); Tourist zones = 2 (max. summer excess +21% (Nkhotakota (Central Region))); Lit area = +8.6% (annual growth; population +2.7%/yr)

facts.title: Recommendations
facts.text: • Use night-time lights as a leading and subnational indicator, as a complement to — never a replacement for — the national accounts. • Publish regional GDP estimates as experimental statistics, with intervals and a methodological note, after comparison with available regional accounts. • Cross-check the map of populations “in the dark” against grid-connection registers: the average gap with the World Bank access rate is +18 percentage points. • Document breaks detected without an associated event (sensor change, outage, local event) before any economic interpretation. • Have the 2 isolated sites checked on high-resolution imagery and complete the official register of industrial zones used as the validation reference. • Monitor the light of industrial clusters monthly as a leading indicator of industrial output, and compare it with the industrial production index where one exists. • Publish the tourist season index right after the summer (VIIRS data are available within weeks), ahead of hotel-night statistics, and recalibrate it on them every year. • Cross newly lit areas with urban plans and grid-connection registers to tell planned expansion, informal settlements and rural electrification apart. • Update the dashboard every quarter (monthly VIIRS series) and every year (annual VNL composites).

facts.title: Limitation: What lights measure
facts.text: Upward radiance emitted around 01:30: agriculture, daytime trade, poorly lit services and the rural informal economy are poorly captured.

facts.title: Limitation: Saturation and blooming
facts.text: DMSP saturates in city centres (DN 63) and “blooms” beyond lit areas; VIIRS is much better, but blooming still inflates the lit area of cities.

facts.title: Limitation: Gas flares and isolated sites
facts.text: The automatic mask may remove isolated mines, ports or power plants, and miss small flares; candidates are exported for verification.

facts.title: Limitation: Clouds, seasons, moon
facts.text: Cloudy months are only partially observed; STL removes average seasonality but not an abnormal season (snow, late monsoon).

facts.title: Limitation: Product breaks
facts.text: DMSP and VIIRS are not directly comparable: the harmonised long series (Li et al., 2020) is a modelled product, to be read for trends only.

facts.title: Limitation: NTL–GDP elasticity
facts.text: Estimated on 10 to 30 annual observations: wide intervals, possible instability, a non-causal relationship that varies with the level of development.

facts.title: Limitation: Access to electricity
facts.text: “Inhabited without light” ≠ “not connected”: a connected household with low consumption is invisible; the indicator depends strongly on the radiance threshold and the population data.

facts.title: Limitation: Administrative boundaries
facts.text: geoBoundaries/GAUL may differ from official boundaries; small ADM2 units are sensitive to light spilling over from neighbouring units.

facts.title: Limitation: Industrial zones
facts.text: Detection relies on thresholds: a power plant, a port or a large shopping centre can meet the signals; a dimly lit factory without visible emissions is missed. Sentinel-5P (≈ 5 km) and MODIS (1 km) are coarser than VIIRS: NO₂/SO₂/heat signals describe a neighbourhood, not a building.

facts.title: Limitation: Summer tourism
facts.text: The summer excess captures any rise in summer light (second homes, diaspora visits, festivals, construction), not only tourism; at high latitudes, very short summer nights reduce VIIRS observations. Ramadan changes night-time activity: the summers concerned are flagged.

facts.title: Limitation: Urbanisation
facts.text: The lit area depends on the detection threshold and on light blooming around cities; a connected but dimly lit neighbourhood stays invisible. Population (GHSL/WorldPop) is modelled from censuses: its growth is not an independent observation, and years between two epochs are interpolated.

facts.title: Central Region (ADM1)
facts.text: Central Region (ADM1, 2025): share of national light 48.4%, annual growth +5.9% (CI +3.7% to +8.2%, class Growth), light per capita 0.045, population 0.47 M, in the dark 66%, estimated GDP (experimental) 5.90 bn USD.

facts.title: Southern Region (ADM1)
facts.text: Southern Region (ADM1, 2025): share of national light 40.4%, annual growth +3.6% (CI +0.1% to +5.4%, class Growth), light per capita 0.039, population 0.45 M, in the dark 68%, estimated GDP (experimental) 4.92 bn USD.

facts.title: Northern Region (ADM1)
facts.text: Northern Region (ADM1, 2025): share of national light 11.2%, annual growth +6.9% (CI +5.3% to +8.8%, class Growth), light per capita 0.034, population 0.14 M, in the dark 61%, estimated GDP (experimental) 1.36 bn USD.

facts.title: ADM2: ranking
facts.text: 28 ADM2 units. Classes: Growth 25, Stagnation 3. Fastest growth: Dowa (Central Region) (+12.6%), Nkhotakota (Central Region) (+12.1%), Chitipa (Northern Region) (+11.9%), Chiradzulu (Southern Region) (+10.6%), Ntchisi (Central Region) (+9.1%), Rumphi (Northern Region) (+8.9%), Likoma (Northern Region) (+8.7%), Phalombe (Southern Region) (+8.7%). Slowest: Balaka (Southern Region) (+1.4%), Blantyre (Southern Region) (+1.6%), Thyolo (Southern Region) (+1.9%), Karonga (Northern Region) (+3.3%), Mchinji (Central Region) (+3.6%), Zomba (Southern Region) (+3.7%), Mwanza (Southern Region) (+4.0%), Machinga (Southern Region) (+4.1%).

facts.title: ADM2: brightest
facts.text: Brightest units: Lilongwe (Central Region) (34.7%), Blantyre (Southern Region) (21.7%), Mzimba (Northern Region) (6.4%), Mangochi (Northern Region) (4.7%), Zomba (Southern Region) (3.0%), Chikwawa (Southern Region) (2.9%), Nkhotakota (Central Region) (2.4%), Kasungu (Central Region) (2.4%), Dowa (Central Region) (2.2%), Salima (Central Region) (1.9%).

facts.title: Convergence and concentration
facts.text: β-convergence (ADM2): β = -0.023 (CI -0.032 to -0.014, n = 27). β < 0 with a fully negative CI = convergence. Share of the leading region: 51.7% in 2014 → 48.4% in 2025; HHI 0.410.

facts.title: Elasticity (levels)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in levels: β = 1.43 (95% CI 0.75 to 2.11, R² = 0.69, n = 12, confidence medium: n = 12, significant but wide CI (1.36)). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Elasticity (growth rates)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in growth rates: β = 0.56 (95% CI -3.44 to 4.56, R² = 0.01, n = 11, confidence low: n = 11, not significant (p = 0.78)). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Elasticity (long DMSP–VIIRS series)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in long DMSP–VIIRS series: β = 1.06 (95% CI 0.72 to 1.40, R² = 0.83, n = 30, confidence high: n = 30, p < 0.01, narrow CI). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Out-of-sample tracking
facts.text: Out of sample, light-based growth has a correlation of -0.22 with official growth; mean absolute error 2.2 percentage point.

facts.title: Shock: COVID-19
facts.text: COVID-19 (2020-03-01 → 2021-06-30): trough of 2.6% on 2020-09-01, back to the pre-shock level after 7 months. Distinguishable from noise: no.

facts.title: Detected breaks
facts.text: Structural breaks: 2015-11-01 (5.9 %); 2017-02-01 (35.5 %); 2021-04-01 (13.4 %). Without a known event within ±6 months: 2.

facts.title: Regional impact of shocks
facts.text: Hardest-hit regions (trough): Central Region -21.5 % (covid19), Northern Region -0.4 % (covid19), Southern Region 0.8 % (covid19).

facts.title: Gini and Theil
facts.text: Gini of light per capita (ADM2): 0.491 in 2014 → 0.424 in 2025 (change -0.067, bootstrap CI -0.114 to 0.008). Theil T 0.308; between-region share 3%.

facts.title: Population in the dark
facts.text: People in inhabited areas without detectable light: 0.39 M (71%) in 2014 → 0.52 M (66%) in 2025. Urban/rural light-per-capita ratio 1.8. Proxy of electricity access, sensitive to the threshold.

facts.title: Comparison with the World Bank
facts.text: Average gap between the share of people in lit areas and the World Bank electricity-access rate: 17.5 points.

facts.title: Industrial zones: summary
facts.text: 20 industrial clusters (≥ 3 of 6 signals): Heavy industry 11, Business park & logistics 6, Isolated site to verify 2, Oil, gas & flares 1. Share of national light: 14.0%; annual growth +2.2%. Validation (OpenStreetMap): precision 55%, recall 27%.

facts.title: Main industrial clusters
facts.text: IND-001 — Isolated site to verify in Blantyre (Southern Region) (65.36 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-004 — Business park & logistics in Lilongwe (Central Region) (3.655 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-002 — Heavy industry in Mzimba (Northern Region) (6.235 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-007 — Business park & logistics in Lilongwe (Central Region) (1.935 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-005 — Heavy industry in Nkhotakota (Central Region) (3.225 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-011 — Business park & logistics in Lilongwe (Central Region) (1.72 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-006 — Business park & logistics in Lilongwe (Central Region) (1.935 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-003 — Heavy industry in Mzimba (Northern Region) (3.655 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-010 — Oil, gas & flares in Karonga (Northern Region) (1.72 km², 3 signals, confidence low); IND-009 — Heavy industry in Chikwawa (Southern Region) (1.935 km², 4 signals, confidence medium)

facts.title: Industry — Southern Region
facts.text: Southern Region: 8 industrial cluster(s), 73.7 km², 25.2% of the region's light.

facts.title: Industry — Central Region
facts.text: Central Region: 6 industrial cluster(s), 13.8 km², 5.1% of the region's light.

facts.title: Industry — Northern Region
facts.text: Northern Region: 5 industrial cluster(s), 14.0 km², 11.4% of the region's light.

facts.title: Industrial light and value added
facts.text: Correlation between the growth of industrial light and of industry value added (World Bank, NV.IND.TOTL.KD): 0.07 over 11 years.

facts.title: Tourism: tourist zones
facts.text: 2 tourist zone(s) out of 28 ADM2 units (net summer excess ≥ 10%, peak months [12, 1]): Nkhotakota (Central Region) (+21%, confidence medium), Mzimba (Northern Region) (+12%, confidence medium).

facts.title: Validation with hotel nights
facts.text: Correlation between the season index and international tourist arrivals (WDI): -0.96 (4 years; in growth rates: n/a).

facts.title: Urbanisation: lit area and population
facts.text: National lit area: +8.6% per year; population: +2.7% per year. Classes (ADM2): Electrified urbanisation 27, Balanced growth 1.

facts.title: Urbanisation: newly lit areas
facts.text: Between 2014 and 2025: 1,743 km² newly lit, of which 489 km² already inhabited (electrification, ≈ 36k people) and 1,254 km² of new settlements; 30 km² lost their light.

facts.title: Urbanisation: units
facts.text: Fastest lit-area expansion: Chiradzulu (Southern Region) (+16.6%/yr), Nkhata Bay (Northern Region) (+15.1%/yr), Nkhotakota (Central Region) (+15.0%/yr), Dowa (Central Region) (+14.6%/yr), Chitipa (Northern Region) (+13.7%/yr), Phalombe (Southern Region) (+12.6%/yr). Unlit growth (population faster than light): none.

facts.title: Validation with GHSL built-up
facts.text: Spearman rank correlation between lit-area growth and GHSL built-up growth: 0.09 (p = 0.664, 28 units).

facts.title: Quality and international standards
facts.text: Night-time-light indicators are experimental statistics: they complement official statistics and do not replace them. Every output is published with its method, validation, uncertainty, limitations and a confidence level. Frameworks applied: UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics, DQAF, UNECE GSBPM, FAIR principles.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Time dynamics
facts.text: Validation: Trend significance (Mann–Kendall) and monthly/annual consistency (p-value = 0.0002). Uncertainty: 95% CI of annual growth: +2.6% to +6.8% Limitations: Cloud cover and short summer nights; light is not value added. Status: experimental statistic; confidence high.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Regional growth and convergence
facts.text: Validation: Rank correlation with tropospheric NO₂ (independent source) (Spearman ρ = 0.15). Uncertainty: Class assigned only if |slope| ≥ threshold and p < α; CI of β (robust errors). Limitations: Small units: noise and light blooming between neighbours. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Light–GDP relationship
facts.text: Validation: Out-of-sample tracking of official growth (correlation / MAE (pp) = -0.22 / 2.2). Uncertainty: 95% CI of the elasticity: 0.75 to 2.11; 80% and 95% prediction intervals. Limitations: Short annual sample; regional GDP is an experimental statistic to be checked against regional accounts. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Shocks and resilience
facts.text: Validation: Does the trough exceed ordinary variability? (trough (main shock) = 2.6% — no). Uncertainty: Pre-shock month-to-month variability (robust SD); unexplained breaks flagged. Limitations: Shocks hitting poorly lit activities (agriculture, daytime services) are underestimated. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Inequality and electrification
facts.text: Validation: Gap with the World Bank electricity-access rate (mean gap (pp) = 17.5). Uncertainty: Range across radiance thresholds; bootstrap CI of the Gini. Limitations: Proxy of outdoor lighting, not of connection: a connected but dimly lit household looks “in the dark”. Status: experimental statistic; confidence medium.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Industrial zones
facts.text: Validation: Comparison with the reference list (OpenStreetMap) (precision / recall / F1 = 55% / 27% / 0.36). Uncertainty: Per-cluster confidence from the number of strong signals; isolated sites to verify. Limitations: Sentinel-5P (≈ 5 km) and MODIS (1 km) resolution: signals describe a neighbourhood. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Seasonal tourism
facts.text: Validation: Correlation with international tourist arrivals (WDI) (r = -0.96). Uncertainty: p-value per unit; 2020–2021 excluded from the classification. Limitations: Any summer activity (diaspora, second homes, festivals) is captured, not only tourism. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Quality sheet — Urbanisation signals
facts.text: Validation: Rank correlation with GHSL built-up area growth (independent source) (Spearman ρ = 0.09). Uncertainty: Persistence required over two years to limit noise; ± 1 pp margin between growth rates before classifying. Limitations: Light measures outdoor lighting, not urbanisation in the administrative sense; blooming widens cities; GHSL population is interpolated between epochs. Status: experimental statistic; confidence low.

facts.title: Method — Method
facts.text: Data: VIIRS DNB monthly (VCMSLCFG) and annual VNL V2, harmonised DMSP–VIIRS, daily Black Marble, GHSL/WorldPop, Sentinel-5P NO₂/SO₂, MODIS LST, World Bank. Cleaning: pixels valid if cf_cvg ≥ 2, unit-month kept if ≥ 80% of pixels observed, spikes replaced, background and gas flares masked.

facts.title: Method — Dynamics
facts.text: Dynamics: robust STL on log(sum of lights), Theil–Sen trend + Mann–Kendall test, year-on-year growth, breaks by piecewise-linear segmentation with a BIC penalty.

facts.title: Method — Regions
facts.text: Regions: robust growth per unit, Growth/Decline class if |slope| ≥ 1%/yr and p < 0.10; β-convergence (robust OLS), σ-convergence, Herfindahl index.

facts.title: Method — GDP
facts.text: GDP: log(NTL) = α + β log(GDP) in levels and growth rates, HAC standard errors, DW/BP/JB diagnostics, out-of-sample tracking; experimental regional GDP allocated by light (γ = 1 and 0.5).

facts.title: Method — Shocks
facts.text: Shocks: trough = largest gap to the 12-month pre-shock level of the seasonally adjusted series, recovery = return to that level; daily Black Marble index (7-day rolling median).

facts.title: Method — Inequality
facts.text: Inequality: population-weighted Gini, Theil (between/within decomposition) and Lorenz; population in the dark = residents of pixels ≥ 5 people below 0.5 nW (sensitivity 0.25/0.5/1).

facts.title: Method — Industry
facts.text: Industry: six signals per pixel (light ≥ 5 nW, light per resident, GHSL non-residential built-up, Sentinel-5P NO₂ and SO₂, MODIS surface heat); pixels with ≥ 3 signals grouped into clusters; typology, confidence from concordant signals, precision/recall validation (official list or OSM).

facts.title: Method — Tourism
facts.text: Tourism: summer excess = log(peak-month light / shoulder-month light); net of the median of comparable units at the same latitude; tourist zone if ≥ +10% and significant over ≥ 3 summers; season index base 100; Ramadan flagged; validation with hotel nights.

facts.title: Method — Urbanisation
facts.text: Urbanisation: annual lit area (pixels ≥ threshold) and its growth (Theil–Sen) compared with population growth (GHSL/WorldPop); newly lit areas (dark in the first 2 years, lit in the last 2), split into electrification of already inhabited areas and new settlements; validation with GHSL BUILT-S built-up growth.

tools.name: search_facts
tools.description: Search the published facts (key messages, methods, limitations, national figures) for those answering a question. Use it first for any general question.

tools.name: rank_units
tools.description: Rank regions (ADM1) or districts (ADM2) by an indicator for the latest year: fastest growth, largest share of population in the dark, etc.

tools.name: unit_profile
tools.description: Full profile of a region or district: latest indicators, light trend, growth class, industrial and tourist zones.

tools.name: compare_units
tools.description: Compare several units (or the country) on an annual indicator between two years: levels, change and compound annual growth rate.

tools.name: make_chart
tools.description: Draw a chart (annual series of an indicator for units, or a ranking bar chart) shown in the conversation.

tools.name: map_action
tools.description: Drive the dashboard's interactive map: show a year, compare two years (swipe), focus on a unit, or show a layer (lights, population in the dark, indicator, industrial clusters, tourist zones).
